answer: Graph-based trust networks resist Sybil attacks by evaluating each agent as a topological vertex. Bounded random walks from verified anchors force an attacker to incur the verifiable cost of cultivating authentic, multi-party transaction histories to cross graph cuts. Whether agents manage an oasis microgrid or measure irradiance at peak zenith, disconnected clusters cannot amplify influence. However, this mechanism penalizes legitimate newcomers due to severe bootstrapping friction.
